section_style_guide.purpose: Provide the basis of preparation and “how to read this report” guidance for IFRS S1/S2 sustainability-related financial disclosures. Establish scope, reporting boundary, connectivity to financial statements, key qualitative characteristics, and the approach to comparatives, estimates, judgements, and cross-referencing.
section_style_guide.tone: Formal, standards-aligned, precise, and neutral. Use assurance-like phrasing that emphasizes completeness, neutrality, accuracy, and freedom from material error. Use cautious, risk-aware language for sensitive matters and forward-looking judgements. Avoid promotional or celebratory language; keep emphasis on methodology and governance of reporting.
section_style_guide.level_of_detail: High-level principles plus practical mechanics. Provide enough detail to explain how disclosures were prepared, scoped, and connected to financial reporting, without duplicating detailed topic disclosures. Use short subsections to cover each general requirement topic explicitly.
section_style_guide.paragraph_style: Start with a short scope and basis-of-preparation statement. Follow with a bulleted list of qualitative characteristics and preparation principles. Then explain standards alignment and how disclosures map to the core pillars (governance, strategy, risk management, metrics and targets). Use short, numbered subsections for specific general requirements (e.g., connected information, comparatives, timing/location, reporting entity/value chain, sources of guidance). Include clear cross-references to where details are located elsewhere in the report set.
section_style_guide.sentence_style: Declarative, unambiguous sentences. Prefer active voice where responsibility is clear; use passive voice sparingly for standard-setting or externally defined requirements. Define terms before use. Keep sentences short-to-medium length; use parallel structure in lists. Use conditional language for estimates and forward-looking information (e.g., “may,” “could,” “is expected to,” “is subject to”).
section_style_guide.preferred_evidence_style: Ground statements in references to applicable standards and internal reporting constructs (e.g., alignment with financial reporting boundary, policies, methods, and estimates). Use traceability via internal cross-references to other sections/appendices rather than embedding extensive evidence artifacts. Clearly flag when contextual information extends beyond the reporting period and why it is included.
section_style_guide.table_usage: Use tables sparingly. Prefer bullets for principles and mechanics. Use compact tables only when they improve scanability (e.g., mapping of general requirements topics to where disclosures appear; summary of applicable standard components; grouped stakeholder categories; stepwise methodology overview). Keep tables simple, with short labels and line breaks for narrow layouts.
section_style_guide.figure_usage: Optional. Use simple diagrams or tile/grid layouts only to summarize scoping elements, stakeholder groupings, or priority themes at a high level. Avoid complex visuals in this section; prioritize clarity and navigability.
section_style_guide.pdf_layout_usage: Use a chapter opener block with a prominent section marker and title. Repeat the section title as a running header on subsequent pages. Maintain consistent margins and line spacing. Use whitespace to separate narrative from list blocks. Format cross-references inline (e.g., “Refer to …”) and keep them consistent. Ensure subsection headings are visually distinct and support scanning.
section_style_guide.how_to_discuss_missing_data: State transparently when information is not available, incomplete, or still under development. Explain the reason (e.g., data limitations, boundary constraints, methodology maturity), the interim approach used (e.g., estimates, proxies, partial coverage), and the plan to improve (e.g., controls, systems, scope expansion). Clarify whether omissions could be material and how materiality was assessed. Avoid implying certainty where estimates are used.
what_to_avoid: Any organization-specific names, brands, report titles, or proprietary program names
Any specific dates, reporting years, edition labels, or publication timing statements
Any amounts, percentages, performance claims, achievements, awards, or comparative boasting
Any jurisdiction-specific legal commentary, incorporation history, or regulatory endorsement narratives
Any specific currencies, geographic footprint details, entity counts, or segment/product descriptions
Any committee names, role titles, or stakeholder labels that are unique to a particular organization
Any fixed list of external frameworks or tools presented as universally applicable; keep configurable
Any specific note/appendix numbering or identifiers; use generic cross-reference placeholders
Exact copied wording from any reference report

recommended_subsections: Statement of alignment with IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards
Reporting boundary and value chain considerations
Materiality approach (financial materiality and impacts, as applicable)
Estimates, assumptions, and judgements (including forward-looking information)
Timing, location, and accessibility of disclosures
Use of guidance and other frameworks (configurable references)
recommended_order: Statement of alignment with IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards
Reporting boundary and value chain considerations
Timing, location, and accessibility of disclosures

recommended_tables.purpose: Provide a navigational index mapping each general requirement topic to the section(s) where it is addressed.
suggested_columns: Where addressed in this report package
recommended_tables.format_notes: Keep to one page where possible; use concise section references (no specific numbering required).

recommended_tables.purpose: Summarize the reporting entity boundary and how it aligns with financial reporting, including value chain coverage approach.
recommended_tables.format_notes: Avoid entity counts or location details; describe boundary conceptually.

recommended_tables.purpose: Describe the materiality assessment/refresh process in a structured, auditable format.
recommended_tables.format_notes: Use generic inputs (e.g., internal analysis, stakeholder engagement, external context) without naming specific tools or parties.

recommended_tables.purpose: Show stakeholder categories considered in the materiality process in a simple, scannable layout.
recommended_tables.format_notes: Use generic category labels; avoid organization-specific role titles.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Visually show how the report content is organized across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics/targets.
recommended_figures_or_diagrams.format_notes: Simple four-quadrant or flow layout; include generic pointers to where each pillar is covered.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Illustrate how financial materiality and impact considerations inform topic prioritization and risk/opportunity management.
recommended_figures_or_diagrams.format_notes: Use a simple two-axis or layered diagram; avoid listing company-specific topics.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Provide a high-level, non-exhaustive visual summary of priority themes identified through materiality.
recommended_figures_or_diagrams.format_notes: Use generic placeholders or theme categories; avoid copying any specific topic set.

recommended_pdf_blocks.content: Section marker + section title + one-sentence purpose statement.
recommended_pdf_blocks.layout_notes: Minimal text; strong hierarchy; ample whitespace.

recommended_pdf_blocks.content: Section title repeated on content pages.
Bulleted list of qualitative characteristics and preparation principles.
recommended_pdf_blocks.layout_notes: Hanging indents; consistent bullet style; wrap long bullets cleanly.

recommended_pdf_blocks.content: Inline “Refer to …” statements directing readers to detailed disclosures elsewhere.
recommended_pdf_blocks.layout_notes: Use consistent phrasing and formatting; avoid specific appendix numbering.

required_narrative_blocks: Scope and basis of preparation (what the section covers and how to use it)
Statement of alignment/adoption with IFRS S1/S2 (and scope of applicability)
Qualitative characteristics and preparation principles (completeness, neutrality, accuracy, clarity, comparability, verifiability, timeliness)
Connectivity to general-purpose financial statements (how boundaries, policies, methods, and estimates are aligned or reconciled)
Reporting boundary and value chain coverage approach (what is included/excluded and why)
Comparatives and consistency (how prior-period information is treated and how changes are explained)
Estimates, assumptions, and judgements (including treatment of forward-looking information)
Connected information and cross-referencing approach (how information is linked across the report package)
optional_narrative_blocks: Materiality approach overview and refresh cadence (process-focused, non-promotional)
Continuous improvement statement (future enhancements framed as planned methodology maturation)
output_structure_rules: Use hierarchical numbering for subsections (e.g., 1.1, 1.2) aligned to IFRS general requirement topics.
Begin with scope/basis of preparation before any methodology detail.
Separate principle statements (what) from mechanics (how) using headings and short paragraphs.
Use bullets for lists of principles, steps, and scoping decisions; avoid dense multi-clause paragraphs.
Include cross-references where detail is located; do not duplicate detailed disclosures in this section.
Explicitly flag contextual information that falls outside the reporting period and explain its purpose.
When describing alignment with financial reporting, state the nature of alignment and note any exceptions.
Avoid fixed external framework lists; present as “may include” or “as applicable” configurable references.

section_specific_no_copying_rules: Do not reproduce any specific reporting period wording; use placeholders such as “the reporting period” and “the reporting date.”
Do not include any specific appendix/note identifiers; use generic cross-reference labels (e.g., “see relevant section/appendix”).
Do not replicate any specific list of priority topics/themes; generate a company-agnostic placeholder approach or omit.
Do not include any jurisdictional endorsement or legal compliance narrative beyond generic statements of applicable requirements.
Do not include any organization-specific stakeholder role titles; use generic stakeholder categories only.
Do not include any claims of being a first/early/voluntary adopter as an achievement; if relevant, describe adoption status neutrally as an implementation context.
quality_checks_for_generation: Neutrality check: no promotional adjectives, awards, or achievement framing.
Standards alignment check: references to IFRS S1/S2 are accurate and positioned as basis-of-preparation, not performance claims.
Completeness check: includes scope, boundary, connectivity, comparatives, estimates/judgements, and cross-referencing approach.
Traceability check: cross-references are present where detail is elsewhere, without using specific note/appendix numbering.
Consistency check: terminology for boundary, reporting period, and qualitative characteristics is used consistently throughout.
Forward-looking caution check: estimates and judgements use appropriately qualified language and describe key assumptions at a high level.
Missing data check: any limitations are explicitly stated with reason, interim approach, and improvement plan.
Company-specific content check: no names, locations, dates, amounts, percentages, tools/vendors, committee names, or unique claims appear.
Readability check: subsections are short, numbered, and scannable; bullets are used for steps and principles.
